sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Legacy setup and file locations
sections.what: Sets up the imports and records where this file lives and where the unified checker is. The header also lists the newer commands to use instead.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the old wrapper pointing at the new checker so older commands still work.
sections.watch_out: The unified checker must sit in the same folder, or every run fails.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Forwarding the request to the unified checker
sections.what: Passes the command arguments to the unified checker. When no file names are given, it adds the slides type so only slide files are checked, then passes the checker's exit code back.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the old behavior while the real work moves to the new checker.
sections.watch_out: Any word that does not start with a dash counts as a file name, including values after flags such as `--type`, so the slides default is skipped in those cases.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Running only when started directly
sections.what: Runs the wrapper only when this file is started directly from the command line.
sections.why: Likely reason: a standard Python pattern so other code can import the file safely.

summary: An old-style command that passes slide checks on to the unified HTML token checker and returns that checker's result.
purpose: Keeps older commands and habits working after validation moved into html-token-validator.py.
why: The file header calls it a legacy wrapper, so it was kept for compatibility. Likely reason: older users and scripts still call this name.
how: 1. Receive the command arguments. 2. If no file names are given, add the slides type. 3. Run the unified checker with the same Python program. 4. Exit with the same success or failure code it returns.
inputs: Command arguments, such as file names or option flags.
outputs: Whatever the unified checker prints, plus its success or failure code.
risks: If the unified checker is moved or renamed, every run fails with an error. Any option change in the unified checker automatically affects this wrapper.
debug: If the wrapper fails right away, check that html-token-validator.py sits in the same folder. To see what actually runs, run the unified checker directly with the same options. Missing slide files appear as errors from the unified checker.
